rungs.title: Present tense: I & you
rungs.teach:
Darija builds the present with a **ka-** prefix, and the prefix already says who: **kan-** = I, **kat-** = you. So the pronoun is optional — the verb carries it.

• kanakol = I eat
• katakol = you eat

Take any verb you know and put kan-/kat- on the front.

**Two sentence habits** (don't overthink these): lead with the verb and drop the subject — *bghit atay* = (I) want tea — and put adjectives **after** the noun — *atay skhun* = tea hot = hot tea.

rungs.title: Saying not: ma … sh
rungs.teach:
To negate a verb, **wrap** it: **ma** before, **sh** after.

• kanfhem = I understand → **ma** kanfhem**sh** = I don't understand
• bghit = I want → **ma** bghit**sh** = I don't want

This one line — ma kanfhemsh — is your most useful sentence in the country.

rungs.title: Asking questions
rungs.teach:
Two ways to ask:

1. **Front a question word:** fin (where), shhal (how much/many), ash (what), fuqash (when), kifash (how), shkun (who).

2. **Yes/no?** Put **wash** at the front of a statement.

• fin l-ħammam? = where's the bathroom?
• wash kayn atay? = is there tea?

quiz.prompt: Turn “kayn atay” (there is tea) into “is there tea?”

rungs.title: Talking about later: ghadi
rungs.teach:
For “going to / will”, put **ghadi** in front of the verb (still with its kan-/kat- prefix, or just the bare verb).

• ghadi nmshi = I'm going to go
• ghadi nakhod hada = I'll take this one

One little word buys you the whole future. No tense to memorize.

quiz.prompt: Which word makes it future (“going to”)?

rungs.title: Understanding “he/she/it”: kay- / kat-
rungs.teach:
You mostly need to *recognize* this, to follow what people tell you. The same ka- present, other people:

• **kay-** = he/it → kayn = there is (lit. “it exists”)
• **kat-** = she → katmshi = she goes

You won't produce these much — but you'll hear them constantly in answers.
